title: Count Special Quadruplets
summary: For a 0-indexed integer array, count the unique quadruplets (a, b, c, d) where the sum of the first three elements equals the fourth, and the indices are in ascending order.
statement: For a 0-indexed integer array, count the unique quadruplets (a, b, c, d) where the sum of the first three elements equals the fourth, and the indices are in ascending order.
constraints: nums has 4 through 50 positive integers, each at most 100.
Count index tuples a<b<c<d for which nums[a]+nums[b]+nums[c]=nums[d].
hints: Sweep b backward while counting right-side differences for valid c,d pairs.
Add each new d-minus-c to a counter, then query it for every a<b.
At each b the counter contains exactly pairs b<c<d, so matching left sums enumerates every valid ordered tuple once.

tests.explanation: The four indices satisfy one plus two plus three equals six, so one tuple counts.
No increasing four-index tuple satisfies the equation.
